name: vscode-colorize
description: Visualize CSS colors with legacy Colorize behavior plus first-class Lua and FiveM support.

scripts.check: node --check src/extension.js && node --check src/color-parser.js && node --check src/release-updater.js && node --check src/updates.js

colorize.updates.autoUpdate.description: Check stable GitHub releases daily and install verified updates automatically. Reload VS Code when prompted to activate them. Disable to update manually with Colorize Plus: Check for updates.

colorize.languages.description: Language identifiers in which colors are decorated. Lua is enabled by default.

colorize.include.description: Legacy Colorize glob patterns for including files and folders.

colorize.exclude.description: Legacy Colorize glob patterns for files and folders that must not be colorized or scanned for variables.

colorize.files.description: Additional glob patterns kept for compatibility with earlier Colorize configurations.

colorize.files_extensions.description: File extensions supported in addition to language identifiers. Kept for compatibility with Colorize.

colorize.ruler_decoration.description: Show detected colors in the editor overview ruler (scroll bar), as in the original Colorize extension.

colorize.colorized_colors.description: Color syntaxes to display. Legacy Colorize syntaxes are preserved and extended with LUA and FIVEM.

colorize.colorized_variables.description: Variable families whose references inherit the color of their declaration.

colorize.enable_search_variables.description: Scan matching workspace files for CSS, Sass, Less and Stylus color variables so references work across files. Disabled by default to preserve Colorize Plus startup performance.

colorize.hide_current_line_decorations.description: Hide decorations on every active selection line.

colorize.lua.enableTables.description: Colorize Lua RGB/RGBA tables, including color = { r = 0, g = 170, b = 255, a = 150 }.

colorize.lua.enableFiveM.description: Colorize FiveM caret codes (^1) and ~ color codes (~r~) inside Lua strings.
